record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: What is the maximal possible number of cusps on a rational cuspidal plane curve?

evidence.quote:
PROBLEM 2. Find the maximal number of cusps among all the rational cuspidal
plane curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A plane curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ is called a rational cuspidal plane curve if it is irreducible, its normalization is isomorphic to $\mathbb{P}^1$, and every singular point of $C$ is a cusp (a locally irreducible singularity, i.e. an analytic branch with one place). Let $N(C)$ denote the number of cusps (singular points) of such a curve, and define
$$M = \sup\{ N(C) : C \subset \mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}} \text{ is a rational cuspidal plane curve}\}.$$
Determine the exact value of $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is still open in its exact form. K. Tono proved that a rational cuspidal plane curve has at most 8 cusps, and Orevkov later refined this bound. The largest known examples have 4 cusps, and it is conjectured the maximum equals 4, but this has not been established.

status_evidence.title: On the Number of the Cusps of Rational Cuspidal Plane Curves (Piontkowski)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bounds on the number of cusps of rational cuspidal plane curves.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds on cusp number have been established but exact maximum remains open.

status_evidence.title: Remark on Tono's theorem about cuspidal curves (Orevkov)
status_evidence.snippet: Improves Tono's bound that the number of cusps of a rational cuspidal plane curve is at most 8.
status_evidence.claim: Tono's upper bound of 8 cusps; the question of the actual maximum remains open.

status_evidence.title: Rational Cuspidal Curves (Moe thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys known constructions; the largest known examples have 4 cusps.
status_evidence.claim: Maximum known is 4 cusps; conjectured to be the sharp value.
